fields: Six Islands by Speedboat with Snorkelling and Dolphin Watching
A speedboat day from Hurghada taking in six islands, three snorkelling stops and a walk out on a sandbank.

A speedboat day that leaves at half past eight and runs about eight hours. The route takes in six islands, among them Giftun, Nemo Bay, Orange Bay, Magawish and the sandbank at Abu Minqar, where you can walk out on the sand. Three snorkelling stops are made along the way, one of them over a wreck, and there is dolphin watching off Giftun.

Island entrance fees sit in the price, together with snorkelling gear, a life jacket, a guide, soft drinks, water, seasonal fruit and a shaded area on board. Lunch is not part of this option: a lunch or a seafood lunch on the island can be added when you book, and so can a wetsuit, a GoPro video, a banana boat ride or a twister ride. Bring a towel, sunscreen and some cash for the day.

Orange Bay Cruise with Two Snorkelling Stops and Lunch
Eight hours from Hurghada: two snorkelling stops, two hours on Orange Bay Island and a buffet lunch on board.

A full day at sea with a long stop at Orange Bay. The coach collects you from your hotel in Hurghada at eight, and the boat sails out for the first of two snorkelling stops with an instructor and the gear.

Two hours on Orange Bay Island follow, the entry covered, then a buffet lunch with salads and fruit and unlimited juice, cola, tea and coffee. The boat has toilets and showers. Drinks on the island and photos are not included. Children have their own price.

Six Islands by Speedboat with Dolphin Watching
Eight hours by speedboat from Hurghada: Giftun, Nemo Bay, Orange Bay, Magawish, White Island and Abu Minqar, with three snorkelling stops.

A full day around the islands off Hurghada. The car collects you from your hotel at half past eight, and the speedboat spends two hours in the Giftun National Park area looking for dolphins and snorkelling. Dolphins are wild, so no boat can promise a sighting.

The day goes on to Nemo Bay, Orange Bay, Magawish Island, a sandbank and Abu Minqar, with a snorkelling stop at a wreck, and the entrance fees for Orange Bay, White Island, Magawish and Abu Minqar are in the price, with soft drinks, water and fruit. Lunch is not included. Children have their own price.

Dolphin House by Speedboat from Hurghada
Four hours by speedboat: two snorkelling and swimming stops at Dolphin House, with the gear, water, soft drinks and fruit.

A quicker way to Dolphin House. The car collects you from your hotel in Hurghada, and the speedboat runs out to the reef in about an hour, with shade on board.

An hour and a half at the reef gives two guided stops to snorkel and swim, where dolphins often feed and rest. Dolphins are wild, so no boat can promise a sighting. The gear, life jackets, water, soft drinks and fruit are in the price; the nature reserve fee is paid on the day. Children have their own price.

Dolphin House Morning Cruise with Breakfast
Five hours from Hurghada: two forty-minute snorkelling and swimming sessions at Dolphin House, breakfast on board and unlimited drinks.

An early cruise from Hurghada to the Dolphin House reef. The car collects you from your hotel, and the boat takes about an hour to reach the reef, where dolphins often feed and rest. Dolphins are wild animals, so no boat can promise a sighting, and swimming near them depends on the sea and on how many boats are there.

There are two forty-minute sessions of snorkelling and swimming, with breakfast on board between them and a guide for non-swimmers. The gear, tea, coffee, soft drinks and water are in the price; the nature reserve fee, towels and underwater photos are not. Children have their own price.

A five-hour yacht day from Hurghada, with a morning and an afternoon departure. The car collects you from your hotel, and the yacht sails to the Dolphin House reef, where dolphins often feed and rest; if they are there and the sea allows, you can swim near them. Dolphins are wild, so no boat can promise a sighting.

There are two guided snorkelling stops, at Dolphin House and a smaller reef nearby, with the gear included. A breakfast buffet and a seafood lunch are served on board, with hot and soft drinks. Towels, underwater photos and tips are not included. Children have their own price.

Dolphin House by Speedboat
A short speedboat run out to the Dolphin House reef, with snorkelling over the coral.

The Dolphin House is a horseshoe reef out from Hurghada where spinner dolphins rest through the day, and a speedboat reaches it fast enough to make the trip four hours rather than a whole day.

The boat makes two guided snorkelling and swimming stops at the reef, with the equipment and life jackets aboard. Water, soft drinks and seasonal fruit are served on the boat, and there is a shaded area on deck. Pickup from your hotel in Hurghada and the drive back are included.

Six Islands by Speedboat
A full day by speedboat around six islands off Hurghada, with three snorkelling stops and the island entry fees.

Six islands in a day is a speedboat’s kind of trip: the hull is quick enough between them that the day is spent at the stops rather than on the way to them. The route takes in Orange Bay, White Island, Magawish, Abu Minqar and a sandbank, with the entry fees for them in the price.

There are three guided snorkelling stops, one of them over a wreck, and the gear and life jackets are aboard. Drinks and seasonal fruit are served on the boat, the captain watches for dolphins in the open water between the islands, and pickup from your hotel in Hurghada is included. Lunch is not part of this price.

Wadi El Gemal Jeep Safari with a Bedouin Dinner
Seven hours from Marsa Alam: Wadi El Gemal National Park by jeep, a desert spring, Cleopatra’s Temple and a Bedouin dinner.

An afternoon and evening in Wadi El Gemal National Park, south of Marsa Alam. The jeep collects you from your hotel at noon and drives into the park.

The stops are a panorama over the valley, an acacia and an arak tree, a water spring and the ruins of Cleopatra’s Temple, and the day ends with a Bedouin dinner before the drive back. The team confirms the order of the stops when it confirms your booking. Children have their own price.

Marsa Mubarak and Small Shenwa Snorkelling with a Meal
Four and a half hours from Marsa Alam: two guided snorkelling stops, a meal on board and a walk around Port Ghalib Marina.

A short boat day on two reefs north of Marsa Alam. The bus collects you from your hotel, and the boat reaches Marsa Mubarak in about half an hour.

The guides lead two snorkelling stops, at Marsa Mubarak and Small Shenwa, where turtles and dugongs live; they are wild, and no boat can promise a sighting. An open buffet lunch or dinner is served on board, and the day ends with a walk around Port Ghalib Marina. Snorkelling gear is not included. The team confirms the pickup time after booking. Children have their own price.
